answer: Work waits on the karst until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the jade of the next round. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The design leans on reputation decay for idle identities, reset on any identity-link attempt, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain. Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name. The umber of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
